description: National US transport networks: Census TIGER 2024 primary roads and rail lines, BTS NTAD North American Rail Network links/nodes, National Highway Freight Network and intermodal freight facilities, USACE principal ports (CY2023 tonnage) and waterway network, MARAD strategic seaports, NGA World Port Index and OpenFlights airline routes; the sampling block keeps the bounded San Francisco Overpass excerpt

source.publisher: US Census Bureau (TIGER/Line); USDOT BTS (NTAD); USACE; MARAD; NGA (World Port Index); OpenFlights
source.license_notes: TIGER/Line, NTAD, USACE, MARAD and NGA Pub. 150 are US federal government works (public domain). OpenFlights routes.dat is ODbL 1.0 (attribution, share-alike for public derived databases) and frozen around June 2014; it describes topology, not current schedules.
source.release: TIGER 2024; NTAD/USACE ArcGIS feature services queried 2026-09-15 (counts in acquisition.description); NGA Pub 150 current; OpenFlights master

setup: Use regional extracts; specialized PBF/GIS parser needed. Preserve licenses and network topology.

sampling.criteria: First 100 highway ways in a small San Francisco bounding box; tags and center only, not full network geometry.

normalization.entity_identity: source IDs, canonical geography, explicitly labeled unresolved references and aggregate cohorts

acquisition.description: One shard per file or ArcGIS GeoJSON page (2,000 features ordered by OBJECTID, WGS84, 5-decimal coordinates; long lines/polygons generalized with maxAllowableOffset=0.0001 deg). Layer counts at configuration time: ntad_rail_lines=302771, ntad_rail_nodes=250202, ntad_nhfn=12989, usace_principal_ports=150, usace_waterway_nodes=6255, usace_waterway_links=6859, marad_strategic_seaports=18, ntad_intermodal_rail_tofc_cofc=241, ntad_intermodal_marine_roro=84, ntad_intermodal_liquid_bulk=640, ntad_intermodal_pipeline_terminals=1401, ntad_intermodal_air_to_truck=404. Each layer lists one trailing page beyond the count so modest growth is still captured; regenerate the list if a layer grows by more than 2,000 features.
